sources.read: Methods 3, evaluation 4.1, tables and adverse cases
sources.finding: Executable harness optimization around a frozen policy, auxiliary tools and retained memory already overlap a generic improvement loop. Held-out scene/task improvements do not imply weight learning. Some solutions bypass the VLA. RoboCasa scenes and specialist LIBERO-Pro examples tie or worsen.
sources.consequence: Compare whole effective systems and competent harness baselines; do not call orchestration or memory Nisayon's novelty.

sources.read: Sections 4.3–4.7, development timing and feedback protocols
sources.finding: Eight real tasks, executable skills and richer feedback overlap persistent robotic experimentation. Sequential reviewer phases differ in transition counts and median delay; they do not isolate a reviewer causal effect. The small feedback study has one development session per task/arm and excludes separate evaluation time. Verification failures can resemble controller failures.
sources.consequence: Do not add agents without measured benefit. Include acquisition, review and evaluation in cost. Distinguish correcting the oracle from improving the robot.

sources.finding: Proposed memory lifecycle and writer isolation are distinguished from archived enforcement. Repeated-frontier efficacy conclusions are withdrawn because route schedules differ and semantic labels are unvalidated. A competent grounded single agent succeeds on a hard slice. Selected stale-route cases do not establish net benefit or false-withdrawal rates.
sources.consequence: Keep unknown decisions unresolved while retaining only justified partial evidence. Test actual enforcement, unchanged controls and a capable native comparator.

sources.read: Problem formulation, graph/skill/simulation methods; project site; current execution/checkpoint source
sources.finding: Typed executable graphs and simulator rehearsal assume a known fixed workcell, robot and sensors, known objects and bounded pose ranges. This is a scoped automation setting, not unrestricted generalist transfer. Existing skills and auxiliary controllers are part of the system.
sources.consequence: Explicit assumptions are useful, not novel graph architecture. Effective executor configuration belongs in dependency scope.

code.head: 53e8049d1e30aa2b55e941914361fca645694e87
code.observation: Common task/seed evaluation launch; recorded wall duration is not full authoring/review cost. Init states cycle modulo their available count. Checkpoint predicates use privileged state, distinguish probes/hard checks, and retain evaluation errors. Authored predicate execution is not independent empirical verification.

sources.read: III, VII, VIII; project validation levels; Arena runner source
sources.finding: Defines feasible task-preserving variation and records executions. Human-authored graphs sharing skills/perception/planning are a stronger comparator than a generic coding agent without the skill library. Generated graphs remain below human graphs in the reported Newton conditions. Stateful sequences use whole-instance units; cycle-time summaries use successful trials and are not complete costs.
sources.consequence: Equal semantic tools and correct sample units are essential. Simulation variants differ in assets/rendering/robot details; their agreement is not independent physical confirmation.

code.head: 64b594ed2e1ae25e431d235de086c7cfd99d9aaf
code.observation: Runner enforces Newton backend and changes actuator decimation, solver capacity, rendering and runtime registrations. File identity alone omits effective environment unless those dependencies are declared.

sources.read: Announcement, release qualifications and linked GR00T project
sources.finding: GR00T 2, Isaac Lab 3.0, Arena 0.4 developer preview and GaP/VABAR demonstrate an active ecosystem around evaluation and harness improvement. Completing 40 of 50 tasks at least once is not an 80-percent rollout success rate.
sources.consequence: Do not build a competing generic simulator or claim throughput differentiates Nisayon.

sources.finding: Project reports a 40-percent zero-shot trial result and 95-percent few-shot result under its protocols, and lists code availability in December. These differ from the announcement's at-least-once task count.
sources.consequence: Treat as author-reported results with differing denominators and currently limited replication availability.
sources.gap: Whitepaper https://research.nvidia.com/labs/gear/gr00t-2/assets/gr00t2_whitepaper.pdf was not read: web tool rejected its 23,457,173-byte size. No whitepaper-method or replication claim.

sources.read: Workflow and scaling account; not a reproduced benchmark
sources.finding: Composable task variation and parallel closed-loop evaluation already address evaluation throughput.
sources.consequence: Throughput is a comparator capability, not evidence of lower total qualification work.

sources.read: Automated screening, human review methodology and failure categories
sources.finding: Automated screening and expert human inspection reveal underspecified and defective coding-evaluation tasks. Human adjudication concentrates on flagged tasks; it does not validate every unflagged case. Passing tests or another model's verdict can still miss intended semantics.
sources.consequence: Review task/oracle validity before interpreting execution as success; preserve false or unresolved conclusions instead of averaging them away.

sources.read: Cohorts, verbalized-awareness measures, associations and system-cue intervention
sources.finding: In the reported agent safety cohorts, evaluation and production behavior differ. An intervention changes the specified evaluation objective and strongly shifts performance. Expressed reasoning measures do not expose all latent beliefs, and a six-model association does not establish universal transfer.
sources.consequence: Instructions, harness, population and context can affect applicability. A matched benchmark score is not deployment acceptance.

sources.finding: An early experimental world model supports interactive simulated worlds under restricted access. The article does not establish the physical transfer error bounds needed for Nisayon task confirmation.
sources.consequence: World-model rollouts may propose tests; they cannot automatically replace required empirical confirmation.

sources.read: Robotic demonstration and surrounding claim scope
sources.finding: The reported cornhole demonstration and simulation-to-real account do not supply a prospective population and complete-cost counterfactual for Nisayon's decision problem.
sources.consequence: Do not extrapolate selected demonstrations into general safety or economic superiority.

limit: Retained primary-source and selected code review; author-reported results are not Nisayon replications. No exhaustive survey or competitive ranking.
